questions.question: Describe a custom industrial control-panel project you developed at General Electric. How did you take it from power-circuit design and schematic development through manufacturing support, inspection, and functional testing?
What specific steps do you use to design a UL 508A-compliant control panel, including component selection, short-circuit considerations, wiring, labeling, and documentation?

Tell us about the power-draw and thermal calculations you have performed for control panels. What inputs did you use, how did the results affect the design, and how did you validate the finished panel?

This role requires review of electrical construction documents and shop drawings. What do you look for when reviewing electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, bills of material, and panel assembly documentation?

Describe your experience performing functional and thermal testing using load banks and data-recording equipment. How did you define acceptance criteria and address failures identified during testing?

What experience do you have with hazardous-location standards, including IEC 60079 and UL, CSA, or Intertek certification processes? How would you apply that experience to industrial facility projects?

Describe a project where you led or coordinated engineering, manufacturing, quality, or certification activities across multiple stakeholders. How did you manage documentation, schedule, technical decisions, and quality requirements?

What is your experience developing control logic, embedded controls, or data-acquisition systems? Please describe the automated X-ray Tube Tester or another relevant system, including sensors, control hardware, software, and validation.

How have you used electrical design software such as SolidWorks Electrical, Altium, or similar tools to produce schematics and wiring documentation? What is your familiarity with AutoCAD, and how would you adapt to AutoCAD-based facility construction documents?

This position involves electrical systems for water and wastewater facilities, including power distribution, motor control, PLC systems, lighting, conduit, wiring, startup, and NEC compliance. Which portions of this work align most closely with your industrial control-panel background, and how would you approach supporting facility testing and startup?
